Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were not willing.
And look, your house is left to you [?]
the one who comes in the name of the Lord.
And Jesus came out of the temple and was going away, and his disciples approached him to show him the temple buildings.
He answered them, “Do you see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be torn down.”
As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”
Jesus answered them, “Be careful that no one deceives you.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will deceive many.
You will hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for all these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.
All these things are the beginning of birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to suffering and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.
Then many will fall away, betray one another, and hate one another.
Many false prophets will arise and deceive many.
Because lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the inhabited world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
then those who are in Judea must flee to the mountains.
Anyone on the housetop must not come down to take what is in his house.
Likewise, anyone in the field must not turn back to take his clothes.
But woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days!
Pray that your flight will not be in winter or on the Sabbath.
For then there will be great suffering, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the whole world until now, nor ever will occur again.
If those days had not been shortened, no one would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the chosen.
Look, I have told you beforehand.
So if they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
For just as lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.
Immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will grow dark, and the moon will not give its light. The stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear, coming on the clouds of heaven with his great power.
He will send his angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn this lesson from the fig tree: when its branch is already tender and its leaves sprout, you know that the harvest is near.
So you too, when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day and that hour, not even the angels of heaven, but only the Father alone.
For just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the day of the Son of Man.
For in the days before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
They did not realize it until the water came and swept them all away. So it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding at the millstones; one will be taken and the other left.
Therefore keep watch, because you do not know at what hour your Lord will come.
But know this: if the master of the house had known during which watch of the night the thief would come, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
For this reason, you too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.
Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom the master will put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that wicked servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’
and begins to [?] his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards,
that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know.
He will cut him in two and assign him his place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
For the foolish took their lamps but did not take oil with them.
But the wise took oil in containers along with their lamps.
While the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and slept.
At midnight there was a shout: “Look, the bridegroom is coming! Go out to meet him!”
Then all those virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.
The foolish said to the wise, “Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.”
But the wise answered, “There may not be enough for both you and us. Go instead to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves.”
While they were going to buy it, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the doors were shut.
Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, “Lord, Lord, open the door for us!”
But he answered, “Truly I tell you, I do not know you.”
Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour when the Son of Man will come.
For it is like a man going away who called his servants and entrusted his property to them.
To one he gave four talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to his ability. Then he went away immediately.
The one who had received four talents went and traded with them and gained another four talents.
Likewise, the one who had received two gained another two.
But the one who had received one went and dug in the ground and hid his master's silver.
After a long time, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received four talents came forward and brought another four talents, saying, “Master, you entrusted four talents to me. Look, I have gained another four talents with them.”
His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will put you in charge of much. Enter into your master's joy.”
The one who had received two talents also came forward and said, “Master, you entrusted two talents to me. Look, I have gained another two talents with them.”
His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will put you in charge of much. Enter into your master's joy.”
The one who had received one talent also came forward and said, “Master, I knew that you were a harsh man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter.
So I was afraid and went and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.”
His master answered him, “You wicked, lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter.
Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and when I returned, I would have received what was mine with interest.”
Then he said to his servants, “Take the talent from him and give it
to the one who has ten talents. For the one who has will be given more everywhere, and he will have an abundance. But from the one who does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away.
And throw the worthless servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne.
All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will place the sheep at his right and the goats at his left.
Then the king will say to those at his right, “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the whole world.
For I was hungry, and you gave me food. I was thirsty, and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed me.
I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.”
Then the righteous will answer him, saying, “Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?
When did we see you as a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you?
When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?”
The king will answer them, “Truly I tell you, since you did it for one of these little brothers of mine, the least of them, you did it for me.”
Then he will say to those at his left, “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you gave me no food. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me; naked, and you did not clothe me; in prison, and you did not visit me.”
Then they too will answer, saying, “Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and not serve you?”
Then he will answer them, saying, “Truly I tell you, since you did not do it for one of these least ones, neither did you do it for me.”
These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
And when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
“You know that the Passover takes place in two days, and the Son of Man is being handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
They plotted against Jesus, to seize him by deceit and kill him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”
Now Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper.
A woman came to him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume and poured it on his head as he reclined at the table.
When his disciples saw this, they were indignant and said, “Why this waste?
This perfume could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor.”
But Jesus, knowing this, said to them, “Why are you troubling the woman? She has done a good deed for me.
For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.
By pouring this perfume on my body, she has done it for my burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed throughout the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, “What will you give me if I hand him over to you?” They set out thirty silver coins for him.
From then on he looked for a suitable opportunity to betray him.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My time is near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my disciples.’”
The disciples did as Jesus had instructed them and prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, he reclined at the table with the twelve disciples.
While they were eating, he said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.”
Deeply distressed, each of them began to say to him, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand into the dish with me will betray me.
The Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”
Judas, who betrayed him, said in reply, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You have said it.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.
This is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
But I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”
And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will fall away because of me tonight, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’”
“But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered him, “Even if everyone falls away because of you, I will never fall away because of you.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a village called Gethsemane and said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, he began to be sorrowful and distressed.
Then Jesus said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”
And going a little farther, he fell facedown, praying and saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.”
And rising from prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Could you not keep watch with me for one hour?”
“Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again, a second time, he prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass from me unless I drink it, let your will be done.”
And coming back, he again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.”
“Get up, let us go. Look, the one who betrays me has drawn near.”
And while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with weapons and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
Now his betrayer had given them a sign: “The one I kiss is the man. Arrest him.”
And immediately he approached Jesus.
He said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus, and arrested him.
And one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and struck the high priest’s slave, cutting off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back in its place, for all who take up the sword will perish by the sword.”
“Or do you think that I cannot now appeal to my Father, and he will provide me with more than twelve legions of angels?”
“But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say that it must happen this way?”
At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out with weapons and clubs to arrest me as though I were a robber? Every day I sat with you in the temple teaching, and you did not arrest me.”
But all this happened so that the writings of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.
Those who had arrested Jesus led him to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the servants to see the outcome.
The chief priests and elders and the whole council were looking for false witnesses against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
But they found none, even though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two witnesses came forward
and said, “This man said, ‘I can destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What is this testimony these men are giving against you?”
But Jesus remained silent. The high priest spoke to him again: “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus said to him, “You have said so. Nevertheless, I tell you: from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has spoken blasphemy! Why do we still need witnesses? Look, you have now heard his blasphemy.
What do you think?” They answered, “He deserves death.”
Then they spat in his face and mistreated him, while others slapped him on the cheek,
saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit you?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”
But he denied it before everyone, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.”
When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to him, “This man too was there with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man.”
A little later, those standing nearby came up and said to Peter, “You really are one of them. Your speech gives you away.”
Then he began to curse and swear, “I do not know the man.” Immediately a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered the words of Jesus, who had said to him, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
They bound him, led him away, and handed him over to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
Then Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned. Filled with remorse, he returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.” They said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
And he threw it down in the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver and said, “It is not lawful to put it into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.”
After consulting together, they used it to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for strangers.
For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
Then what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled: “And they took the thirty silver coins, the price of the one whose value had been set, whom the sons of Israel had valued,
and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You say so.”
When the chief priests and elders accused him, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how much they testify against you?”
But he did not answer him, not even a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
At every feast the governor was accustomed to release to the crowd whichever prisoner they wanted.
At that time he had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.
When they had gathered, Pilate said to them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you: Barabbas or Jesus, who is called Christ?”
For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent word to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for today I suffered greatly in a dream because of him.”
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and have Jesus put to death.
The governor said to them in reply, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”
Pilate said to them, “What, then, shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified!”
The governor said to them, “What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the more, saying, “Let him be crucified!”

When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that an uproar was growing instead, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this righteous man’s blood. See to it yourselves.”
And all the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children.”
Then he released Barabbas to them, but he had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the judgment hall and gathered the whole cohort around him.
They stripped him and dressed him in a scarlet cloak.
They wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and placed a reed in his right hand. Kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”
And they spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on the head.
And when they had mocked him, they took the cloak off him, put his own clothes on him, and led him away to be crucified.
As they were going out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. They compelled him to carry his cross.
And they came to a place called Golgotha, which means the Place of a Skull.
They gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink. But after tasting it, he would not drink.
After crucifying him, they divided his clothes by casting lots.
And they sat down and kept watch over him there.
And above his head they placed the written charge against him: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads
and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”
Likewise, the chief priests, mocking him along with the scribes, elders, and Pharisees, said,
“He saved others; can you not save yourself? If he is the King of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe him.
He trusted in God; let God rescue him now, if he wants him. For he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
The two robbers crucified with him also taunted him in the same way.
From the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At about the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lemma zavakhtani,” which means, “God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
Some of those standing there heard this and said, “He is calling Elijah.”
And immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
The others said, “Leave him alone. Let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.” But another took a spear and pierced his side, and water and blood came out.
Jesus cried out again in a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split apart.
The tombs opened, and many bodies of the holy people who had fallen asleep were raised.
And after his resurrection, they came out of the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many.
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were afraid and said, “Truly, this was the Son of God.”
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too was a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered that Jesus’ body be given to him.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
The next day, the day after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
saying, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was still alive, he said, ‘After three days I will rise.’

So order the tomb to be secured until the third day, lest his disciples come at night and steal him and tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’ Then the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go and secure it as best you know how.”
So they went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone and posting the guard.
Late on the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, approached the tomb, rolled the stone away from its entrance, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
The guards shook with fear of him and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
He is not here, for he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where Christ lay.
Go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead. Look, he is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him. See, I have told you.”
They left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy and ran to tell the disciples. As they were going to tell his disciples,
Jesus met them, saying, “Rejoice!” They came up, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me.”
While they were going, some of the guard went into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
The elders gathered, and after taking counsel, they gave the soldiers a large amount of silver,
saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came at night and stole him while we were asleep.’”
And if the governor hears about this, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble.
So they took the money and did as they had been instructed. And this story has spread among the Jews to this day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
And when they saw him, they bowed down before him, but some doubted.
And Jesus came up and said to them, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe everything I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you every day, until the end of the age.” Amen. ✝
